findings.reason: §6 should cite the landed mechanism and narrow itself to whichever part is genuinely still missing, instead of claiming a prerequisite the code already satisfies.
findings.text: §6 states "dispatch must ask the supervisor to launch it from the batch step, which needs a `spawn` request" and "Until it lands, full RESUME must not dispatch from fleet sessions", but the spawn verb is already implemented (reckon/crew/fleet_supervisor.py:1243 dispatches `spawn <run-id> <spec>`, spawn_supervisor at :1114) and dispatch already routes both worker and watcher-producer launch through it (reckon/crew/dispatch.py:9841 `_start_supervisor` -> `_spawn_through_fleet` at :9762, and :1177 for producers)

findings.reason: the plan should extend the placement owner or name why a separate wrapper is required, rather than adopting a parallel placement path as the laptop's entry point.
findings.text: §4 proposes the fixed `Host fleet` alias with `RemoteCommand ~/.local/bin/fleet-shell`, but that 20-line script re-implements placement (hand-parses record.json with `sed` for `job_id` at :12 and `runtime_dir` at :18, then builds its own `srun --overlap --pty`) while reckon already owns a placement entry point (fleet_node.placement_argv and the `reckon fleet-node place` command at reckon/cli.py:638); the plan does not say why fleet-shell cannot call that owner

findings.reason: a reader that re-derives rather than reading the record drifts from the value the supervisor published (fleet-attach's default versus the record's runtime_dir), so the design should route every resolution through fleet_node.recorded_job_id() and the record's runtime_dir — though §2's step 3 safe-discovery rule (find by name, cancel by id) is the right instinct and should keep the record as the single source.
findings.text: `recorded_job_id()` is the owner of reading the fleet record, yet the design resolves the same file independently in three places: dotfiles/bin/cx:227 (`sed` parse of `job_id`), reckon/bin/fleet-shell:12 and :18, and reckon/bin/fleet-attach:12 which instead re-derives the runtime dir as `${FLEET_RUNTIME_DIR:-/tmp/$(id -u)-fleet}` without reading the record's own `runtime_dir`; cx already depends on reckon for the hold (`reckon fleet-node hold`, reckon/cli.py:567)

rubric_items.deep_module: pass — the plan adopts the batch-step supervisor (reckon/crew/fleet_supervisor.py, 1355 lines behind a 1-line exec launcher) as one deep module that hides zellij lifecycle, runtime-dir creation, standing services and the request FIFO behind a one-request-per-line interface.
rubric_items.duplicate_owner: a finding — the design reads ~/.local/state/fleet/record.json in three hand-written places (cx, fleet-shell, fleet-attach) while reckon/crew/fleet_node.py owns it.
rubric_items.interface_budget: pass — public_definitions 0, cli_options 0, mcp_views 0, refusal_families 0; the design adds no new public definition, CLI option, MCP view or refusal family (the `spawn` verb it calls for already exists in fleet_supervisor.py, and CX_FLEET_VIA / ~/.config/cx/fleet-sessions are shell/dotfiles surfaces outside these four families).
rubric_items.reuse_search: a finding — the plan's §6 presents the supervisor `spawn` request and launching dispatch workers from the batch step as outstanding work, but both already exist in reckon.
rubric_items.thin_wrapper: a finding — §4 adopts reckon/bin/fleet-shell as the `Host fleet` RemoteCommand; the 20-line wrapper re-derives the fleet's job and runtime directory by hand-parsing the record rather than extending the module that owns it.
